title: Stream Snapshot Inspector — PRD draft
content:
Context:
This is a working PRD for a "Stream Snapshot Inspector" feature for the Hosted API. The Inspector is a first-class developer surface and runtime protocol that produces deterministic, queryable stream snapshots for (1) offline replay of streaming sessions, (2) structured diagnostics for tool-calls and partial-output fragments, and (3) low-friction SDK integration points that let product teams reproduce and debug problems without heavy production instrumentation.

Problem statement:
- Customers and internal teams struggle to debug intermittent failures and correctness regressions in streaming+tool workflows because:
  - Partial outputs (incremental frames) are non-deterministic across retries and when tool-side effects occur.
  - Error cases are visible only as telemetry metrics or truncated transcripts; reproducing exact client-server interleaving is expensive.
  - SDKs expose streaming tokens in a raw form that requires heavy local scaffolding to replay tool-handshake flows.
- Result: long mean-time-to-resolution for customer incidents, brittle rollouts for streaming SDK features, and slow developer feedback loops for structured-output regressions.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Developer UX: Provide a single click/SDK API that captures a full streaming session snapshot (prefix, tool-call events, partial frames, server routing decisions, kernel/quantization profile metadata).
- Deterministic replay: Replaying a snapshot in a sandboxed runtime reproduces the observed token stream and tool-call sequence 95% of the time for non-randomized models (allowing seeded variants).
- Lightweight: Snapshot capture adds <2% p99 latency and minimal storage cost via compact encoding and optional KV-prefix compression.
- Observability: Snapshots integrate with Console traces and per-route debug traces so SREs and engineers can triage with timeline views and action-step inspection.
- SDK ergonomics: JS and Python SDKs expose capture/replay hooks with a small, idiomatic API surface.

Non-goals:
- Full fidelity of randomized sampling-based model outputs (sampling-dominated runs may not be exactly reproducible).
- Replacing existing audit logs or security traces. Inspector snapshots are for debugging and developer replay, not compliance-grade archiving.

Primary personas:
- Platform engineer (oncall) troubleshooting latency spikes and mis-ordered tool calls.
- SDK integrator (frontend/backend engineer) reproducing client-side crashes relating to incremental frames.
- Product manager validating structured-output regressions across model rollouts.

Key user stories:
- As an oncall, I want to capture a snapshot for a failing streaming session from the Console so I can replay locally and step through tool-call boundaries.
- As an SDK developer, I want a programmatic API to create a snapshot for a session-id and download a deterministic replay bundle for unit tests.
- As a PM, I want a diff view between two snapshots (pre/post rollout) that highlights structural changes in tool-call sequences and schema breaks in typed outputs.

High-level approach / components:
1) Snapshot capture API (runtime):
   - Each streaming session may be marked capture=true via request header or Console toggle.
   - Runtime collects: request metadata, model id + seed, routing decisions, kernel/quantization profile selected, KV cache deltas, incremental output frames (with frame ids and parent ids), serialized tool-call intents and responses, and annotate errors/exceptions.
   - Data is compacted on-the-fly: prefix dedupe, JSONL for frames, gzip + light delta encoding for long transcripts.

2) Snapshot storage & indexing:
   - Short retention (30 days by default) in an encrypted blob store.
   - Index fields: session_id, capture_time, route/model, top-level error code, tool_graph_hash, approximate size.
   - Optional customer-configurable retention and export for Dedicated/Private customers.

3) Replay harness (sandboxed):
   - Deterministic sandbox runtime that can consume snapshot bundles and replay: token generation, tool-handshake simulation, and client-binding frames.
   - Modes: dry-run verification (validate structure), full replay (step through token stream with same seeding), and instrumented run (attach a debugger to inspect frame-level payloads).

4) Console + SDK surfaces:
   - Console: Capture button on request traces, timeline view with collapsible frame groups, diff UI to compare two snapshots, and download link for bundle.
   - JS/Python SDKs: captureSession(sessionId, { reason, includeKV }) and replayBundle(path|buffer, options). Minimal sample code included in this doc.

5) Structured-output validation & diffs:
   - Snapshot inspector runs a set of lightweight schema validators (user-provided JSONSchema for typed outputs) during capture and flags breaks.
   - Diff engine highlights missing/extra fields, changed types, and tool-call reorderings.

API sketches (informal):
- HTTP header: X-Redwood-Capture: true | token
- POST /v1/sessions/{id}/capture -> 200 { snapshot_id }
- GET /v1/snapshots/{snapshot_id} -> meta + download url (signed short-lived)
- SDK JS: await redwood.captureSession(sessionId, { tags: ['oncall'], includeKV: true }) -> returns snapshotId
- SDK Python: redwood.snapshots.replay(local_bundle_path, seed=1234) -> yields frame iterator

SDK ergonomics notes:
- JS API is promise-first with small helpers for streaming frameworks (React/Next, Node streams). Example helper captureStream(stream, opts) that emits a snapshotId when terminal frame is observed.
- Python API is iterator-based and fits into async frameworks (async for frame in replay(...)).
- Backward compatibility: SDKs will default to no-op in older clients; capture is opt-in.
- Minimal footprints: capture helpers are small (single file) so customers can drop into existing apps with one import.

Console UX sketch (notes):
- On a trace, show a "Capture snapshot" action with brief explanation of cost and retention.
- Timeline: vertical swimlanes for client, server tokens, tool invocations, and kernel/quant profile changes.
- Click a frame to see full JSON payload, call stack, and (if available) a replay button that opens the sandbox-runner.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Snapshots may contain user prompts or PII. Default policy: redact user-specified PII via existing redaction pipeline unless tenant explicitly requests full capture and retention.
- Encryption at rest and signed download URLs.
- Access control: only users with trace-level access can download snapshots. Audit log entries for snapshot creation/download.

Success metrics (initial):
- Time-to-fix for streaming incidents reduced by 30% in Q2 pilot.
- 80% of oncall captures are replayable locally without extra instrumentation.
- 500 snapshots captured during beta with <2% increase in median latency on captured routes.

Rollout plan / milestones (6–12 weeks):
- Week 0–2: Spec finalization, API sketches, and dataset/retention policy defined.
- Week 2–5: Runtime capture prototype + minimal storage pipeline. Internal-only.
- Week 5–8: SDK capture helpers + Console capture button (alpha). Invite SRE and platform teams.
- Week 8–12: Replay harness, diff engine, and public beta for a subset of customers.

Risks and mitigations:
- Storage costs: mitigate with compression and sampling policies; default off for high-volume routes.
- Privacy exposure: enforce redaction and tenant-level opt-in for full payloads.
- Replay divergence for sampling models: document limitations; provide seed capture and best-effort deterministic mode.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should we persist model RNG seeds by default or only in debug mode? (seed helps reproducibility but may expose internal sampling logic)
- How much tooling metadata (kernel selection, quant flags) is necessary vs noise? Start conservative and extend.
- Triage UX: is Console the right default for captures, or should we integrate snapshot creation into existing trace-alert rules?

Experiments to validate before full build:
- Capture performance microbench: measure overhead on p50/p95/p99 for representative routes (chat with tools, streaming long prefixes).
- Replay fidelity test: sample 200 captured sessions, run sandbox replay, and measure structure/token alignment.

Developer notes / quick sample (JS):
- const snapshotId = await redwood.captureSession(sessionId, { tags: ['inc-420-failure'], includeKV: false })
- // Later, download and replay: await redwood.snapshots.replay('/tmp/snap-420.bundle', { mode: 'dry-run' })

Appendix: short checklist for eng review:
- [ ] Schema for snapshot bundle (flat list: metadata, frames.jsonl, tools.jsonl, kv-deltas.bin)
- [ ] Console timeline wireframes
- [ ] SDK helper draft in redwood-sdk repo (PR #748)
- [ ] Linear ticket for retention policy (RED-3243)

Notes to self: this is intentionally a small-surface MVP that focuses on reproducibility and developer velocity. The feature should not be advertised as a compliance or long-term archiving tool. Keep capture opt-in and start with an internal beta before enabling tenant exports.
